### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. hereditary spastic paraplegia 5A  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.716)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:2652)

**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic variant in CYP7B1 (COSMIC:MUTATION_DB) —DISRUPTS→ CYP7B1 (HGNC:2652); CYP7B1 (HGNC:2652) —DECREASES→ Accumulation of 25-hydroxycholesterol (CHEBI:30979); Accumulation of 25-hydroxycholesterol (CHEBI:30979) —DISRUPTS→ Sterol biosynthesis and metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-109590); Sterol biosynthesis and metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-109590) —LEADS_TO→ Neuroinflammation (HP:0002452); Sterol biosynthesis and metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-109590) —LEADS_TO→ Spasticity (HP:0001257); Sterol biosynthesis and metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-109590) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249). Pathogenic variants in CYP7B1 lead to loss-of-function, impairing the conversion of 25-hydroxycholesterol to downstream sterols. This results in the accumulation of 25-hydroxycholesterol, which disrupts normal sterol biosynthesis and metabolism. Dysregulation of sterol metabolism contributes to neuroinflammation, spasticity, and intellectual disability, the core phenotypes of both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of distinct causal genes for each disease, or evidence that variants in CYP7B1 do not impair its enzymatic activity or lead to the accumulation of 25-hydroxycholesterol, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Any common variant (AF > 0.01) in CYP7B1 found in gnomAD that is not strongly associated with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the accumulation of 25-hydroxycholesterol or downstream consequences of its dysregulation in sterol metabolism could offer a unified therapeutic strategy for both CYP7B1-associated diseases.

#### 2. cerebrotendinous xanthomatosis  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.421)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-193807, Reactome:R-HSA-211976)

**Proposed mechanism:** CYP7B1 (HGNC:2462) —DISRUPTS→ bile acid synthesis (REACT:R-HSA-3825540); CYP27A1 (HGNC:2467) —DISRUPTS→ bile acid synthesis (REACT:R-HSA-3825540); bile acid synthesis (REACT:R-HSA-3825540) —DECREASES→ cholesterol metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-3825540); cholesterol metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-3825540) —LEADS_TO→ cholesterol accumulation (HP:0002350); cholesterol metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-3825540) —LEADS_TO→ tendon xanthomas (HP:0000990); cholesterol metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-3825540) —LEADS_TO→ cerebral calcifications (HP:0002345). Loss-of-function mutations in either CYP7B1 (associated with a rare disease) or CYP27A1 (cerebrotendinous xanthomatosis) disrupt bile acid synthesis, leading to a broader dysregulation of cholesterol metabolism. This aberrant cholesterol metabolism results in the accumulation of cholesterol and its precursors, manifesting as phenotypes such as tendon xanthomas, cerebral calcifications, and general cholesterol accumulation.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in CYP7B1 and CYP27A1 do not affect bile acid synthesis or cholesterol metabolism, or that the observed phenotypes arise through entirely independent molecular pathways. _(variant: Identification of common variants (AF > 1%) in gnomAD within the coding regions of CYP7B1 or CYP27A1 that do not segregate with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding this shared pathway disruption in sterol metabolism offers potential therapeutic avenues. Modulating cholesterol metabolism or enhancing bile acid synthesis could be explored as a common treatment strategy for both conditions.

#### 3. congenital bile acid synthesis defect 2  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.420)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-193807)

**Proposed mechanism:** CYP7B1 (HGNC:2594) —DISRUPTS→ Intermediate of bile acid synthesis; Intermediate of bile acid synthesis —DECREASES→ Bile acid metabolism pathway (PW:...); Bile acid metabolism pathway (PW:...) —LEADS_TO→ Cholestasis (HP:0001383); AKR1D1 (HGNC:374) —DISRUPTS→ Intermediate of bile acid synthesis; Intermediate of bile acid synthesis —DECREASES→ Bile acid metabolism pathway (PW:...); Bile acid metabolism pathway (PW:...) —LEADS_TO→ Liver damage (HP:0001377). Loss-of-function mutations in CYP7B1 (causing MONDO:0013439) and AKR1D1 (causing congenital bile acid synthesis defect 2) disrupt distinct steps in the bile acid synthesis pathway. The cumulative impairment in bile acid metabolism leads to overlapping phenotypes such as cholestasis and liver damage.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathways downstream of CYP7B1 and AKR1D1 that do not converge on bile acid metabolism or shared downstream effectors would falsify this hypothesis. Additionally, the absence of shared phenotypes like cholestasis or liver damage in individuals with pathogenic variants in these genes would also serve as falsification. _(variant: N/A)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared downstream consequences of defects in bile acid synthesis, despite originating from different genes, can inform therapeutic strategies for related liver diseases. Targeting common metabolic intermediates or pathways affected by these defects could offer a unified approach to treatment.

#### 4. cholestasis, progressive familial intrahepatic, 5  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.419)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-192105, Reactome:R-HSA-193807, Reactome:R-HSA-211976)

Loss-of-function mutations in CYP7B1 disrupt bile acid synthesis, leading to cholestasis and jaundice. NR1H4 (FXR) regulates bile acid synthesis, and its dysregulation can exacerbate cholestasis.

**How to falsify it:** The absence of mutations in CYP7B1 or NR1H4 in patients diagnosed with these conditions, or the discovery of distinct molecular pathways driving the diseases independently. _(variant: Exome Variant Server (EVS) or gnomAD data showing a high allele frequency (>0.1%) for pathogenic variants in CYP7B1 or NR1H4 in the general population would challenge their causal role.)_

**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-211976)

**Proposed mechanism:** CYP7B1 (HGNC:2403) —DISRUPTS→ Steroidogenesis and bile acid synthesis (REACT:R-HSA-1909701); Steroidogenesis and bile acid synthesis (REACT:R-HSA-1909701) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); Steroidogenesis and bile acid synthesis (REACT:R-HSA-1909701) —DECREASES→ Glucocorticoids (CHEBI:24001); POMC (HGNC:9190) —DISRUPTS→ Pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) processing and signaling (REACT:R-HSA-1909701); Pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) processing and signaling (REACT:R-HSA-1909701) —LEADS_TO→ Obesity (HP:0005101); Pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) processing and signaling (REACT:R-HSA-1909701) —DECREASES→ Alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (α-MSH) (CHEBI:17637); Glucocorticoids (CHEBI:24001) —INCREASES→ Steroidogenesis and bile acid synthesis (REACT:R-HSA-1909701); Alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (α-MSH) (CHEBI:17637) —DECREASES→ Pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) processing and signaling (REACT:R-HSA-1909701).
